The SAVE Act is one of those issues that hits close to home for so many of us—because at the end of the day, your vote is personal. It's the one moment every few years when you get to say, "This is what matters to me, my family, my community." Whether you're a lifelong Democrat worried about keeping voting accessible, a Republican focused on making sure the system is rock-solid, or a No Party Preference voter just wanting fairness, we all want our ballot to count and reflect what we truly believe.

Picture this: You stand in line (or fill out your mail ballot at the kitchen table), thinking about your kids' future, your neighborhood's safety, the country we love. That single act of voting feels powerful because it's yours—no one else's. But if even a small number of non-citizen registrations slip through, it can quietly dilute that power for every citizen. The SAVE Act is a simple, common-sense fix: When you register to vote in federal elections, show proof you're a U.S. citizen—like a birth certificate, passport, or other accepted document. Not at the polling place when you vote—just once, at registration. Once verified, you vote normally under your state's rules. It includes options for folks without the usual paperwork, so it's not about blocking eligible people—it's about building trust that only citizens are on the rolls.

Polls tell us this resonates deeply across lines: Around 83% of Americans support requiring proof of citizenship for registration, including strong majorities of Democrats, Republicans, and independents. It's not a "red" or "blue" idea—it's an American one. We already follow basic checks for driver's licenses, jobs, or flying; why not protect the heart of our democracy the same way?

Yet in California's 18th District, Rep. [NAME] voted against this twice—once in 2024 and again in 2025. Those "No" votes feel out of step with what most of us want: elections we can all believe in.

My wife and her family came here chasing the American Dream—the same dream that draws hardworking people from all over. I admire that spirit. And because I love this country, I want our elections to honor every citizen's voice without question.

Democrats: You've always stood up for making sure no one is unfairly left out. Let's make registration secure so every eligible person's vote carries full weight.

Republicans: You prioritize integrity and accountability. This is a practical way to deliver that trust.

NPPs and everyone in between: You cut through the noise and just want things to work fairly. This does that.

We don't need to agree on everything to agree here: Protecting your vote protects all of us. It's about faith in the system, love for our families and communities, and belief in America's promise. Let's find that common ground, support the SAVE Act, and keep moving forward together as one nation.
